Spelunky 2 (2020) — Mossmouth (Derek Yu)

Genre: Platformer Roguelike | Perspective: 2D Side-scrolling | Players: 1–4 Local + Online | Steam Rating: 92% Positive

🎮 Core Concept

Explore procedurally generated caves, collect treasure, avoid traps, and survive. Pure skill-based roguelike — no meta-progression. Every pixel is dangerous, and the game's systemic interactions create emergent chaos.

👤 Characters (20+)

Character choice is mostly cosmetic with minor starting item differences:

  • Ana Spelunky — Default, balanced
  • Margaret Tunnel — Alt start
  • Colin Northward — Alt start
    • 17 more unlockable characters
  • Secret characters — Found through hidden means

🔫 Combat & Tools

Weapons

Weapon How to Get Behavior
Whip Default Melee attack, destroys pots, triggers arrows
Shotgun Shopkeeper/drop Powerful ranged, knockback on player
Freeze Ray Shop/drop Freezes enemies (then throw/stomp)
Crossbow Shop/drop Long-range single shot
Boomerang Shop/drop Returns after throw
Machete Shop/drop Short-range melee
Mattock Shop/pickup Mines through terrain
Teleporter Shop/pickup Random teleport (DANGEROUS)
Plasma Cannon Rare drop Massive explosion (destroys terrain)

Tools & Items

  • Ropes — Vertical traversal (limited supply)
  • Bombs — Terrain destruction, enemy damage (limited supply)
  • Paste — Bombs stick to surfaces
  • Climbing Gloves — Stick to walls
  • Spring Shoes — Higher jump
  • Spike Shoes — Stomp kills enemies
  • Jetpack / Hoverpack — Flight (game-changers)
  • Cape — Slow fall + glide

🧩 Systemic Interactions (Core Innovation)

The magic of Spelunky is in its systems interacting:

  • Drop a torch → Oil on ground ignites → Fire spreads → Destroys shop → Shopkeeper attacks
  • Whip an arrow trap → Arrow fires → Hits enemy → Enemy drops item → Item triggers another trap
  • Use bomb near water → Water flows → Drowns enemies → Fills lava
  • Throw a dead body at a mine → Mine explodes → Creates new path

🗺️ World Structure

Dwelling (1-1 to 1-4) →
  ├─ Jungle (2-1 to 2-4) → Olmec (boss)
  └─ Volcana (2-1 to 2-4) → Olmec (boss)
→ Tide Pool / Temple of Anubis (3-1 to 3-4) →
→ Ice Caves (4-1 to 4-4) →
→ Neo Babylon (5-1 to 5-4) → Tiamat (boss)
  └─ Sunken City (6-1 to 6-4) → Hundun (7-1)
     └─ Cosmic Ocean (7-1 to 7-99, "endless" loop)
  • Secret areas: Black Market, Duat, Abzu, Eggplant World, City of Gold

📈 Progression — Pure Skill

In-Run

  • Bombs, ropes, items from shops/crates
  • Gold for shop purchases
  • Companion NPCs (hire from coffins/shops)
  • Mount animals (turkeys, axolotls)

Meta-Progression: NONE

  • No permanent upgrades
  • No unlockable power
  • Shortcuts can be built (skip worlds) but with worse loadout
  • Knowledge and skill ARE the progression
  • This is the original roguelike philosophy

🌟 Key Innovations

  1. Systemic Emergent Gameplay — Every element interacts; chaos emerges from simple rules
  2. No Meta-Progression — Pure skill mastery; knowledge is power
  3. "Authored Randomness" — Templates + rules create levels that feel designed despite being procedural
  4. shopkeeper AI — Aggressive NPC that hunts you across floors if angered
  5. Cosmic Ocean — Near-infinite looping endgame (7-1 to 7-99)
  6. Community Mysteries — Hidden paths and secrets took months for the community to discover

❤️ What Players Love

  • "Every death teaches you something — true skill mastery"
  • "The systemic interactions create stories no developer could script"
  • "Fair difficulty — when you die, it's always your fault"
  • "The secrets run impossibly deep — community still discovering things"
  • "Multiplayer is pure hilarity — accidental friendly fire everywhere"

  • Average run: 15–30 minutes
  • Metacritic: 91/100 (PS4)
  • Design philosophy: Knowledge = progression
